title: Myasthenia gravis: drugs to avoid or use with caution

pearls: Sheikh 2021: may be offered cautiously in mild/stable MG with blepharospasm or cervical dystonia — slow titration, close monitoring
entries.title: Botulinum toxins
effect: Distant weakness mimicking MG; can unmask subclinical MG or worsen controlled MG — including after cosmetic doses
sources: Sanders DB, et al. International consensus guidance for management of myasthenia gravis. Neurology 2016;87:419-425, supplemental Table e-2: Drugs to avoid or use with caution in MG

mechanism: Immune — no direct effect on neuromuscular transmission
pearls: Onset typically ~6–7 months after starting (range 1 month–8 years)
~70% remit 6–10 months after stopping
AASLD 2022 lists MG among very late penicillamine adverse effects
saferAlternatives: Wilson disease: trientine — chelator alternative, may be better tolerated (AASLD 2022, statement 16); zinc for asymptomatic or maintenance therapy (statements 17–18) — hepatology decision
entries.title: D-penicillamine
effect: Induces de novo autoimmune MG in ~1–7% of treated patients — usually mild/ocular, ~80% AChR-Ab positive
sources: Sanders DB, et al. International consensus guidance for management of myasthenia gravis. Neurology 2016;87:419-425, supplemental Table e-2: Drugs to avoid or use with caution in MG

mechanism: Reduces miniature endplate potential/current (pre- or postsynaptic)
pearls: MGFA: use cautiously, if at all
Common ED/hospitalist empiric choice for UTI and CAP — check the MAR on every MG consult
saferAlternatives: Penicillins — generally considered safe; rare case reports (ampicillin, amoxicillin)
TMP-SMX, clindamycin, nitrofurantoin — no exacerbations reported
Tetracyclines (e.g., doxycycline) — no clinical reports of worsening
entries.title: Fluoroquinolones
effect: Worsening reported 15 min to 5 days after starting; one series averaged a 10-point rise in QMG score
sources: Sanders DB, et al. International consensus guidance for management of myasthenia gravis. Neurology 2016;87:419-425, supplemental Table e-2: Drugs to avoid or use with caution in MG

effect: Exacerbation and MG-like weakness even in non-MG patients — worst with high doses, renal failure, or concurrent neuromuscular blockers

mechanism: Reduces presynaptic ACh release and postsynaptic sensitivity
pearls: MGFA: IV magnesium potentially dangerous — only if absolutely necessary, then observe
ICG 2016 and Gilhus 2024: magnesium sulfate not recommended for eclampsia/preeclampsia in MG; ACOG 2020 lists MG as a contraindication to MgSO4
Watch automatic electrolyte-replacement protocols
Oral magnesium (milk of magnesia, citrate, oxide) is not addressed by ICG 2016, MGFA or Sheikh 2021 — this caution is for IV magnesium and repletion
saferAlternatives: Eclampsia seizure control in MG: barbiturates or phenytoin (ICG 2016); benzodiazepines or phenytoin (ACOG 2020) — with obstetrics
entries.title: Magnesium (IV and repletion)
effect: Crisis reported after magnesium for preeclampsia and after inpatient repletion
sources: Sanders DB, et al. International consensus guidance for management of myasthenia gravis. Neurology 2016;87:419-425, supplemental Table e-2: Drugs to avoid or use with caution in MG

pearls: Onset usually within ~6 weeks (range 2–12) of starting; risk may be higher with combinations
Look for myositis/myocarditis overlap — worse prognosis (Sheikh 2021)
Decisions on continuing ICI belong to oncology + neurology
entries.title: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
effect: De novo MG (~0.24% of treated patients) or flare of known MG (~85% in one series, half to MGFA class IV–V)
Respiratory failure ~45%, mortality 25–40% in one series; myositis overlap up to 40%, myocarditis rare but potentially fatal

pearls: MGFA: procainamide — use with caution
Sheikh 2021: avoid class Ia agents or use with extreme caution
Propafenone (Ic) has also worsened MG within hours

effect: Procainamide: respiratory failure in MG; MG-like weakness in non-MG patients with renal failure

effect: Worsening of MG; chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine can also induce MG

Controlled studies of IV/oral propranolol showed no significant change in strength or RNS decrement (Sheikh 2021)
Well-controlled MG: usually acceptable at the lowest effective dose with monitoring
entries.title: Beta-blockers
effect: Transient worsening reported
Ophthalmic timolol: rarely increases weakness in MG — the label warns despite topical use

pearls: Not in ICG 2016 Table e-2 or the MGFA list — case reports only (Sheikh 2021)
Amlodipine and diltiazem are not addressed by any source on file
Controlled verapamil studies showed no significant change
Well-controlled MG: lowest effective dose with monitoring (Sheikh 2021)
entries.title: Calcium channel blockers
effect: Felodipine and nifedipine: exacerbation with positive dechallenge/rechallenge
Verapamil/nifedipine start preceded respiratory failure in severe gMG (confounded)
sources: Sheikh S, Alvi U, Soliven B, Rezania K. Drugs that induce or cause deterioration of myasthenia gravis: an update. J Clin Med 2021;10(7):1537. doi:10.3390/jcm10071537

pearls: MGFA: use cautiously if indicated, at the lowest dose needed
Generally safe; occasionally worsens MG and then needs stopping (Sheikh 2021)
saferAlternatives: Bile acid sequestrants, niacin, PCSK9 inhibitors — not reported to worsen MG (Sheikh 2021)
Ezetimibe: one case report of worsening
entries.title: Statins
effect: Worsening in ~11% of statin-exposed MG patients in one series (1–16 weeks after start); rarely de novo MG
